1.reproduce_code:
# 1. Create an external R script named code.R
# ------------------------------------------------------
cat(
  "# this is code.R\n",
  "x <- 42\n",
  "print(x)\n",
  file = "code.R"
)

# 2. Create a revealjs presentation slides_reveal.qmd
# ------------------------------------------------------
# File: slides_reveal.qmd
---
title: "Embedding with revealjs"
format: revealjs
engine: knitr
---

## Embed!

```{embed, file="code.R"}
```

# 3. Render the revealjs presentation
# ------------------------------------------------------
# In your shell, run:
quarto render slides_reveal.qmd
# Then open slides_reveal.html (or preview in RStudio).  You will see the "Embed!" slide with no code.

# 4. Create a plain HTML document slides_html.qmd
# ------------------------------------------------------
# File: slides_html.qmd
---
title: "Embedding without revealjs"
format: html
engine: knitr
---

## Embed!

```{embed, file="code.R"}
```

# 5. Render the HTML document
# ------------------------------------------------------
# In your shell, run:
quarto render slides_html.qmd
# Then open slides_html.html.  You will see the contents of code.R correctly embedded as a code block.
1.explanation: We create an external script (code.R) and then use the knitr embed engine inside two different .qmd files. The first uses revealjs format (and engine: knitr), and after rendering there is an empty <div data-file> on the slide — no code is shown. The second uses the default HTML format, and the embed chunk successfully shows the code. This minimal example reproduces the bug observed in Quarto 1.2.335 with knitr 1.42 on macOS.
1.bug_scenario: When you include an external R script with the knitr embed engine inside a revealjs slideshow (i.e. a .qmd with format: revealjs and engine: knitr), the slide shows the section header but the <div data-file> is empty and no code appears. In contrast, exactly the same embed chunk in a plain HTML document correctly shows the contents of the external script.
